Contents
The Chief Executive’s Report for South Dublin County Council is 
presented to elected members at each monthly Council meeting.  
Section 136(2) of the Local Government Act 2001, as inserted by 
Section 51 of the Local Government Reform Act 2014, requires 
the Chief Executive to prepare a management report in relation to 
the performance of executive functions, including implementation 
of policy or other matters required by the Council in the exercise 
of its reserved functions, and the provision of services.  It should 
be viewed in conjunction with the various updates provided to Area 
Committee Meetings as well as the quarterly Capital Progress 
Report to full Council as part of the reporting structures to 
assist the elected members with their governance and oversight 
responsibilities.
The report includes important updates and information from 
across our various directorates and departments together with a 
range of key statistics that were developed in conjunction with the 
elected members.  It provides the opportunity to highlight major 
news events and to focus on different areas of our work that may 
not always get the attention it deserves while a selection of images 
from recent events is also included.

IPI award nominations 
The draft Clondalkin Local 
Planning Framework began on 
26 August and will run until 29 
September this year. The draft 
framework reflects national policy 
and local feedback as expert input 
on urban design, conservation, 
green infrastructure, transport 
and environmental assessments 
while a conservation plan, a local 
transport plan and architectural 
conservation area appraisals have 
also shaped the proposals. 
Drop-in clinics providing further 
information will take place in the 
Civic Offices, Clondalkin on 10 
September (2pm to 4pm) and in 
Brú Chrónáin - Round Tower Visitor 
Centre on 17 September (6.30pm 
- 8.30pm) while updates will 
also be shared through our social 
media channels throughout the 
consultation period as we seek to 
shape sustainable future expansion 
of Clondalkin village aligned with 
community needs. 
Submissions can be made through 
our online portal on www.sdcc.e . 
National Planning Framework implementation guidelines
Clondalkin Local Planning 
Framework Consultation
Revised housing supply 
targets have been issued to 
local authorities under new 
National Planning Framework 
Implementation – Housing 
Growth Requirements. These 
guidelines set a revised national 
annual target of 50,000 new 
dwellings nationally up to 2040. 
In addition, provision is to be 
made for up to 50% above the 
revised target for sufficient 
headroom to ensure the targets 
are met. 
This means that a new baseline 
requirement for South Dublin 
of 3,217 new dwellings annually 
up to 2034 and 2,414 new 
dwellings for the period 2035 
to 2040, totalling 47,184 new 
homes. Our current County 
Development Plan provides for 
2,613 new homes annually, with 
current output from our housing 
supply monitor broadly on 
target with approximately 2,500 
new homes being delivered per 
year. 
Local authorities are reviewing 
current zoned land capacity and 
must zone sufficient additional 
land to meet new targets. 
Our Planning Department has 
commenced assessment of 
land capacity and deliverability 
as well as potential future 
development lands to inform 
the anticapted increase in zoned 
lands that will required to 
meet the new higher baseline. 
This will also identify lands 
to support additional housing 
delivery up to 2040 and a 
report on land development 
capacity and recommendations 
to meet the objectives of the 
guidelines will be presented to 
councillors next month. 
SDCC have received four 
nominations for the 2025 Irish 
Planning Institute Awards which 
is the joint highest number 
of nominations for any local 
authority.  
The biennial IPI awards 
celebrate excellence in 
planning across Ireland and our 
nominations this year include 
Work IQ (Commercial Project), 
Tallaght West Parks Project 
(Urban Regeneration), Housing 
Supply Monitor (Research 
and Innovation), and Planning 
Authority of the Year. These 
nominations highlight our focus 
on sustainable development, 
innovation and staff support 
and we look forward to the 
awards ceremony at Clontarf 
Castle later this month. 
Planning and Transport
Tallaght Village Plaza
Improvement works to Tallaght 
Village were completed in July 
to address uneven paving caused 
by tree roots. The project saw 
trees replaced with planted beds 
and new buff paving installed to 
create a more aesthic and vibrant 
public space. 
The project was delivered by 
O’Brien Landscaping who will 
maintain the planting for a 12 
month period under the contract 
and we now plan to engage 
further with the local community 
on how to further enhance the 
village and to maximise the 
plaza’s potential.

Mac Uilliam update
New homes for Knocklyon
Management of 51 homes in 
Mac Uilliam estate will revert to 
SDCC following the expiry of a 
lease arrangement with Oaklee 
Housing. Resuming direct 
control of these properties and 
related tenancy management 
will ensure an integrated 
approach to estate management 
in the area providing the 
opportunity for coordinated 
planned maintenance, tenant 
participation initiatives and 
resident association supports 
to be provided across the full 
estate. All tenants currently 
in the properties are being 
informed about the changes 
and are being assured that their 
tenancies remain secure, while 
our housing team is committed 
to providing full support to 
ensure smooth transition. 
In addition, we have recently 
completed extensive upgrade 
works on an apartment block 
on MacUilliam Lane with the 
9 homes there now being 
allocated to applicants from the 
social housing waiting list. 
Part 8 Stocking Avenue
We recently published notice 
of a proposed social housing 
development of 25 homes on 
lands off Stocking Avenue and 
Stocking Lane, Rathfarnham, 
Dublin 16.
The proposed development will 
deliver high-quality, energy-
efficient homes and includes a mix 
of one, two and three bedroom 
houses and apartments. 
Full plans are available on our 
public consultation portal and 
submissions can be made up to 12 
September. 
26 new affordable homes at Swiftbanks, Saggart                   
26 new affordable purchase 
homes are being made available 
at Swiftbanks, a new mixed 
tenure development in Saggart. 
Minimum prices for three-
bedroom homes being offered 
for sale by SDCC are €350,000 
with final prices determined by 
the purchasing power of eligible 
applicants.  
The homes are being made 
available for sale by the council 
in partnership with Cairn Homes 
under an Affordable Dwelling 
Purchase Agreement and are 
available to first-time buyers 
and “fresh start” applicants 
only. Applications must be 
made through our online portal 
before it closes at 4pm on 23 
September.  
The surrounding area offers 
excellent transport links and 
access to schools, shops, 
restaurants, parks and 
recreational amenities - ideal for 
a balanced lifestyle. 
The homes are part of a wider 
developemnt of social and cost 
rental housing being delivered 
by Tuath Housing which offers 
contemporary design, energy 
efficiency and modern living 
spaces. Each home features 
spacious interiors with high 
ceilings, generous storage and 
premium finishes. Sustainability 
is central to the design, with 
double-glazed windows, airtight 
insulation and an advanced 
air-to-water heat pump system, 
achieving A2 BER energy rating. 
Further details on the 
development and how to apply 
are available at: www.sdcc.ie/
en/services/housing/affordable-
homes
Watercourse Grove, a new 
social housing development 
on the Old Knocklyon Road, 
has now been completed 
and is in the process of 
being allocated to eligible 
housing applicants. 
Completed by our 
construction partners 
Cleary Doyle supported 
by SDCC Architectural 
Services, this high-quality 
development consists 
of seven three-bedroom 
houses and nine two-
bedroom apartments and 
provides modern and energy 
efficient new homes that 
will contribute to meeting 
local housing need under 
our housing delivery action 
plan.

Green Ribbon Campaign
#NWED2025
We are proud to support this 
year’s Shine Green Ribbon 
Campaign which aims to end 
the stigma surrounding mental 
health. The theme of this year’s 
campaign ‘Step Up to Stamp 
Out Stigma’, encourages open 
conversations, active listening 
and mutual support. 
While the campaign runs 
throughout the year, September 
is the key month for awareness 
events and activities and SDCC 
staff will mark the month by 
distributing green ribbons and 
wristbands, hosting a coffee 
morning and holding a raffle 
with all proceeds going to a 
suicide prevention charity. 
Mental Health stigma remains 
a signiciant barrier to treatment 
leading to discrimination, social 
exclusion, and a lack of support, 
exacerbating difficulties and 
increasing the risk of loss to 
suicide so every action, big or 
small, helps to create a more 
open and supportive culture 
around mental health. To learn 
more, visit www.shine.ie
South Dublin Hobby Month 
October is Hobby Month in South 
Dublin with events for all interests. 
Brick Con brings Ireland’s largest 
LEGO showcase to the National 
Basketball Arena on 11 and 12 
October, featuring custom builds 
and competitions while Octocon, 
the National Irish Science Fiction 
Convention, takes place at the 
Maldron Hotel in Tallaght the same 
weekend, celebrating sci-fi, fantasy 
and horror. On 4 and 5 October, 
model enthusaiasts can visit the 
IPMS National Exhibition at the 
Spa Hotel in Lucan while Robo 
Riots also promises thrilling robot 
battles at the Basketball Arena. 
Exciting calendar of events at Tallaght Stadium
Dr Mamobo Ogoro, 
CEO of GORM
This autumn is shaping up to 
be one of the busiest and most 
exciting periods at Tallaght 
Stadium, with a packed schedule 
of sporting events taking place.  
On Tuesday 9 September, 
the Republic of Ireland mens’ 
under-21 team take on Andorra in 
a UEFA European Qualifer as they 
look to kick off their campaign 
with a win. Following this, on 
Saturday 13 September, we are 
proud to welcome the Leinster 
Rugby senior team to Tallaght 
where they will face Cardiff in a 
community-focussed pre-season 
friendly with tickets competively 
priced to allow sports fans of all 
ages to enjoy high-quality rugby 
in South Dublin. 
A packed stadium is also 
expected when Shamrock 
Rovers host Bohemians on 26 
September in the Dublin Derby 
- one of the most enticipated 
fixtures in the League of Ireland 
calendar. From October, both 
Rovers and Shelbourne will host 
home UEFA Conference League 
games in Tallaght, welcoming 
a range of European teams 
including Crystal Palace and 
Shakhtar Donetsk. 
In addition, our new stadium 
partners Tallaght Martial Arts 
are busy setting up their facility 
in the ground floor of the north 
stand and will shortly have an 
offical opening. 
Having local, national and 
international teams and fans 
visiting the stadium in the coming 
months will continue to enhance 
Tallaght Stadium as a premier 
venue for sport and community 
engagement. 
This year’s Dublin regional 
event for National Women’s 
Enterprise Day (NWED) will 
take place on Thursday 16 
October in the Radisson 
Hotel, Dublin 8. 
Hosted by Local Enterprise 
Office Dublin City, the 
event celebrates female 
entrepreneurship and provides 
a valuable networking 
opportunity for women in 
business with over 500 
delegates expected to attend. 
LEO South Dublin’s NWED 
ambassador this year is Dr. 
Mamobo Ogoro, CEO of 
GORM, a social enterprise 
that uses inter-cultural media 
and education to connect 
marginalised communities.

Red Line Book Festival 
Colour Dash 2025
The Red Line Book Festival 
returns from 13 to 19 October 
this year, celebrating literature, 
creativity and community across 
South Dublin. Hosted by SDCC 
Libraries, the festival features over 
40 events including author talks, 
workshops and creative sessions 
and our Mayor, Cllr Pamela Kearns, 
will announce full details on 10 
September at an event in the newly 
opened Priory Market in Tallaght.  
Highlights include Illustrator in 
Residence Celina Buckley, leading a 
free five-week workshop series for 
emerging local talent in children’s 
book illustration, culminating in an 
exhibition at Ballyroan Library while 
the bi-lingual poetry competition, 
judged by Aifric Mac Aodha, 
continues to attract entries from 
across the island. Festival events 
will be held at a range of venues 
including The Civic, Rua Red and 
Rathfarnham Castle while selected 
events will feature Irish Lanaguage 
Signing and dedicated bus services 
from library branches. 
Please see redlinefestival.ie for 
more. 
Nominations process for 
presidential candidates
A Presidential Election Order will be 
issued by the Minister for Housing, 
Local Government and Heritage this 
month to confirm the closing date 
for nominations, the polling date 
and other key details relating to the 
upcoming presidential election. 
Potential candidates will then be 
facilitated to address the council at 
a special meeting and if the council 
resolves to nominate a candidate, a 
formal resolution must be adopted 
under Section 16 of the Presidential 
Elections Act 1993, authenticated 
with the council’s seal and sent to 
the Presidential Returning Officer. 
Recognising South Dublin’s rising athletes
Popular Colour Dash is      
back at Corkagh Park
A celebration of sporting 
achievement took place in July 
as sixteen young athletes from 
across the county were recognised 
at the Active South Dublin 
Emerging Talent Bursary awards. 
Athletes ranging from fourteen to 
twenty in age who have already 
made their mark at national or 
international level across a wide 
range of sports including athletics, 
boxing, BMX cycling, karate, 
kickboxing, sailing, taekwondo, 
triathlon and weightlifting were 
awarded financial supports to 
assist their progress as elite 
athletes. 
Funding the bursary was provided 
following a decision by councillors 
to allocate €65,000 in this 
year’s budget with recipients also 
invited to become local sporting 
ambassadors promoting the 
benefits of sport and encouraging 
wider participation in their 
communities. 
Speaking at the event Active 
South Dublin manager 
Thos McDermott noted the 
achievements of the five local 
athletes at last year’s Olympics as 
a source of inspiration and spoke 
about SDCC’s commitment to 
nurturing young sporting talent. 
The recipients of the bursaries 
were: Kate O’Connell, Saoirse 
Fitzgerald, Jack Kelly, Sean 
O’Donnell, Adam Olaniyan, Carly 
Hayes, Calvin McCann, Asha Reen, 
Zoe McDermott, Cillian McArdle, 
Josh Riddell, Amy Wade, Cora 
McNaughton, Ryan Doyle, Aimee 
Carr and Jack Kearney, showing 
the depth and diversity of local 
talent.  
Corkagh Park will burst with 
colour and energy on Saturday 13 
September as the end of summer 
Colour Dash returns. Starting 
at 1pm, the event will welcome 
up to 1,500 participants for an 
afternoon of fun, movement and 
celebration. 
Organised by our Active South 
Dublin team with the support 
from our park rangers and 
events staff, the 2km dash will 
also include a food market and 
entertainment and activities 
organised by staff from our 
libraries and community 
development teams.  
The free event will showcase 
Corkagh Park as well as the 
positive impact of Active South 
Dublin in local communities.

Knockmitten playspace
Friarstown open day
The upgraded playspace at 
Knockmitten Community Centre 
was officially opened on Monday 
25 August by our Mayor, Cllr. 
Pamela Kearns, following the 
completion of enhancement 
works. 
The refurbished area includes 
a wide range of new play 
equipment designed to 
support physical activity, social 
interaction and imaginative play 
with new additions including 
swings, a slide, spinner bowl, 
seesaw, playhouse unit and 
stepping stones. 
The upgrade was funded by a 
grant from the Dept of Rural 
and Community Development 
and the Gaeltacht under the 
Community Recognition Fund 
which also supported the 
recently completed adjacent 
multi-games area. The fund 
supports communities where 
new arrivals to the state have 
been accomodated and this 
project reflects our commitment 
to supporting safe, inclusive, and 
accessibile play facilities. 
Responsible dog ownership
Last month we launched a new 
campaign to promote responsible 
dog ownership and to provide 
practical advice to dog owners. 
An updated leaflet on how to be 
a better dog owner with useful 
information and advice has been 
produced to coincide with the 
campaign and this was distributed 
via social media and at events in 
our parks which were attended by 
various SDCC staff including dog 
wardens, park rangers and litter 
wardens along with our licencing 
and enforcement team. Please see 
www.sdcc.ie for more information. 
Contract signed for delivery of sports pavilions 
Pavilion contract signing
Contracts have been signed with 
ABM Construction Ltd. for the 
design and construction of sports 
pavilions which will see quality 
new changing facilities provided 
for sports participants at Corkagh 
Park and Griffeen Park. 
These pavilions will be modular 
buildings which will comprise 
up to eight dressing rooms and 
storage space and ABM will 
deliver them under a design 
and build contract which 
includes modular manufacture, 
site enabling works, building 
installation and finishes along 
with utility connections and 
landscaping works over a total 
period of approximately twelve to 
fourteen weeks. 
This marks the beginning of 
the roll-out of a wider pavilions 
programme funded by SDCC 
supported by some sports capital 
grants for ten new facilities in 
locations approved by councillors 
under the Part 8 planning 
process. 
A framework agreement is now 
in place to accelerate contractor 
procurement for additional 
pavilions at Arthur Griffith Park/
Griffeen, Collinstown Park, 
Dodder Valley, Kilnamanagh, 
Tymon Park, Sean Walsh Park, 
Kiltipper Park and Willsbrook 
Park. These pavilions are being 
located beside intensively used 
3G and grass pitches in key parks 
and open spaces and facilities 
will also be available to other 
park users for park runs, school 
sports days and other such 
events, supporting health and 
wellbeing and maximizing local 
opportunities for participation 
in our wonderful parks and open 
spaces. 
The eighth annual open day 
at Friarstown Allotments took 
place on Saturday 16 August, 
organised by the South Dublin 
Allotments Association in 
partnership with SDCC. Our 
public realm team provided 
a marquee, competition 
vouchers and goody bags to 
support the event and local 
area committee chairperson 
Cllr. Alan Edge presented 
awards on behalf of the 
mayor, with Tara Holland 
named overall winner and Des 
Garry in second place. 
SDCC Parks were also 
on hand to give guidance 
and assist with judging for 
the event which was well 
attended by plot holders as 
well as councillors and staff.

Local Government Awards:
Local Government Awards:
Nine SDCC Projects Shortlisted
Nine SDCC Projects Shortlisted
Chambers Ireland announced 
the shortlist for the 
2025 Excellence in Local 
Government Awards, held 
annually to recognise and 
celebrate the outstanding 
work being carried out by local 
authorities across Ireland, with 
SDCC shortlisted in nine of 
fifteen categories. 
SDCC has been recognised for 
the following projects:
•	
Ballyroan: A dementia-
inclusive, age friendly 
community in the Age 
Friendly Initiative category
•	
International Protection: 
Fact or Fiction in 
Communications category
•	
Reaching for gender 
equality in local 
government (Diversity & 
Inclusion category) 
•	
Junior Safety Forum 
(Health & Wellbeing 
category) 
•	
Ely Arch: heritage 
conservation through 
public realm design 
(Heritage and Built 
Environment) 
Work IQ nominated in Promoting 
Economic Development Category
•	
Clonburris delivery model 
– Strategic Innovation for 
Sustainable Growth in 
Local Authority Innovation 
•	
Work IQ, innovation centre: 
technology and enterprise 
growth (Promoting 
Economic Development) 
•	
Connecting communities 
through regeneration 
of West Tallaght Parks 
(Supporting Sustainable 
Communities) 
•	
Balancing green and 
growth: delivering 
sustainable development 
and protecting biodiversity 
(Sustainable Environment 
& Biodiversity) 
Award winners will be 
announced at a ceremony 
to be held in November 
in conjunction with the 
Department of Housing, Local 
Government and Heritage, and 
one local authority will also 
be selected as overall local 
authority of the year. 
Colm Ward, Chief Executive 
of SDCC, said: “Today’s 
announcement of the shortlist 
for the Excellence in Local 
Government Awards is 
fantastic news for SDCC and 
we are delighted to see the 
wide range of our projects that 
have been included again this 
year. 
This recognition reflects the 
commitment and dedication 
of our staff, elected members 
and partners to deliver these 
projects and initiatives as we 
continue to create greater 
opportunity for all in South 
Dublin by being a place 
that meets the needs and 
ambitions of everyone here.”

This month sees the long 
awaited completion of 
significant projects to enhance 
the facilities and amenities 
available to the public at both 
Tymon Park and Corkagh Park. 
In Tymon Park, the new 
intergenerational centre at 
the Wellington Lane entrance 
features a café that is designed 
to make the most of its 
parkland setting, with a south-
facing terrace overlooking the 
lake and offering both indoor 
and outdoor seating. It also 
includes a multi- functional 
community space that can be 
divided into smaller rooms if 
needed. 
A thoughtfully considered 
landscape plan integrates the 
centre into the park while its 
green roof and adjacent new 
pollinator planting support 
biodiversity and sustainable 
drainage, contributing to 
the ecological value of the 
park and demonstrates our 
commintment to sustainability. 
The walking route from 
Wellington Lane has been 
upgraded, enhancing 
pedestrian and wheelchair 
access while cycle parking 
has also been provided and 
an attenuation system has 
been added to drain the car 
park to greatly improve flood 
resilience there. 
This follows the reopening of 
the Limekiln section of the 
park with significant progress 
made on the River Poddle 
flood alleviation works, 
providing a new pedestrian 
footpath and boardwalk for 
visitors to enjoy a peaceful way 
to connect with nature, and a 
new integrated constructed 
wetland filters and cleans 
water thereby supporting 
biodiversity and new habitats 
for floral and fauna.  
Over at Corkagh Park, major 
upgrade works have been 
undertaken to create a new 
hub area with a café and 
a multi-use events space 
complete with a stage and 
hard-standing area. Formal 
seating, picnic areas, amenity 
lawn, soft landscaping, 
planting and play areas have 
also been added in this area to 
greatly enhance the amenities 
in the central hub of the park. 
These features provide a 
vibrant and inclusive space for 
park users to enjoy, adding to 
upgrades already provided as 
part of the project including 
the fairy woodland trail and 
upgrades to car parks and 
entrances and we look forward 
to supporting a range of 
community, sports and other 
events to showcase the new 
facilities. 
Our main project partners 
on the works in Tymon 
were contractors James 
Oliver Hearty and Sons and 
consultant design team leads 
Cotter & Naessens Architects, 
while Building Design 
Partnership were project 
consultants for the Corkagh 
project and Mc Avoy Contracts 
Ltd. carried out the civil works 
there, with works overseen by 
SDCC’s parks architectural 
service teams. 
Arrangements are being made 
to open the cafés in both 
parks this month following 
tender processes for operating 
partners. We are delighted to 
announce that O’Brien Event 
Catering Ltd., a local family-
run business who manage 
outdoor catering for a range of 
events and festivals across
Ireland as well as operating 
the successful Café Duomo 
outlet in Firhouse, will manage 
the Tymon intergenerational 
centre including arranging 
bookings for the community 
space there. In addition, the 
café in Corkagh Park will be 
managed by Istimewa Limited,
who currently operate Ruff 
Café at the DSPCA facility 
in Rathfarnham. We look 
forward to working with both 
companies as they expand 
their local business presence 
in facilities that promise to be 
exciting additions to the area 
which we are sure park users in 
both Tymon and Corkagh will 
greatly enjoy!
